title: Dense GEMM vs attention MACs per block, by context length
caption: Packet-owned computation from the block MAC account for a GPT-2 XL-shaped model (width 1,600, FFN 4x): projections+FFN cost 12·S·d^2 MACs and the two attention products cost 2·S^2·d. Attention is a minority below a few thousand tokens, reaches parity at S = 6d ≈ 9,600, and dominates at 16K - the crossover equation plotted. This counts arithmetic only; materialized score storage is the separate quadratic term tiled kernels avoid.

title: KV cache per request vs context (GPT-2 XL, FP16)
caption: Packet-owned computation from the KV-cache formula: 48 layers x 2 tensors x 1,600 wide x 2 bytes = ~307 KB per token per request. The cache is negligible at prompt scale, crosses the ~3 GB FP16 weight footprint near ten thousand tokens, and keeps climbing linearly - multiply again by concurrent requests. Weights stay flat; the cache is the moving term in decode memory.

title: Weight-traffic intensity signatures by lighthouse (FLOP/byte)
caption: Qualitative proxies from the chapter's workload profile: how much arithmetic each family buys per byte of weight traffic in its common regime. Batched ResNet-50 convolutions reuse each weight across ~50K positions and the whole batch; depthwise MobileNetV2 trades some of that reuse away for the ~9x param cut; a batch-one dense layer and GPT-2 decode sit at the GEMV floor. DLRM plots at the floor because lookups are copies - its constraint is capacity, which intensity can't express.
